rules.Policy_Rule_Text:
1) [UHC-MA-2026R8221A-R01] UnitedHealthcare will consider reimbursement for the following procedure code(s) for serum total testosterone when billed for any of the conditions listed below: Procedure Code(s) 84403 Condition(s) a. The monitoring of treatment response in men taking enzyme inhibitors for prostate cancer.

2) [UHC-MA-2026R8221A-R02] UnitedHealthcare will consider reimbursement for the following procedure code(s) for serum total testosterone when billed for any of the conditions listed below: Procedure Code(s) 84403 Condition(s) b. For gender-dysphoric/gender-incongruent persons (baseline, during treatment, and for therapy monitoring).

3) [UHC-MA-2026R8221A-R03] UnitedHealthcare will consider reimbursement for the following procedure code(s) for serum total testosterone when billed for any of the conditions listed below: Procedure Code(s) 84403 Condition(s) c. For symptomatic individuals being evaluated for conditions associated with androgen excess (e.g., polycystic ovary syndrome and functional hypothalamic amenorrhea).

4) [UHC-MA-2026R8221A-R04] UnitedHealthcare will consider reimbursement, subject to the frequency limitations described below, for the following serum total testosterone procedure code(s): Procedure Code(s) 84403 Condition(s) a. For the evaluation of symptoms of androgen deficiency or androgen excess in males. i. Initial screening, one measurement per day, not to exceed two calendar days. ii. If initial screening results are normal and symptoms persist, follow-up testing may be considered no sooner than 60 days after the initial screening.

5) [UHC-MA-2026R8221A-R05] UnitedHealthcare will consider reimbursement, subject to the frequency limitations described below, for the following serum total testosterone procedure code(s): Procedure Code(s) 84403 Condition(s) b. For individuals receiving testosterone replacement therapy. i. No more than once every 60 days.

6) [UHC-MA-2026R8221A-R07] UnitedHealthcare will consider reimbursement of the following procedure codes used to calculate bioavailable testosterone for the condition listed below, based on free and total serum testosterone, sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), and/or albumin. Procedure Code(s) 84403 84410 Condition(s) a. For individuals suspected of having a disorder associated with increased or decreased SHBG levels.

humana.description: Ambulance transport HCPCS A0425-A0427 criteria and modifier requirements.

rules.Policy_Rule_Text: Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow medically necessary ground ambulance and fixed or rotary wing air ambulance services according to Original Medicare guidelines. Humana only reimburses for covered transportation and mileage charges. The amount allowed for transportation includes reimbursement for all other items and services provided. Humana does not make separate payment for such items and services, including but not limited to oxygen, drugs, extra attendants, supplies, electrocardiograms (ECG or EKG) and night differential. Ambulance transportation provided to a member while registered as an inpatient at a hospital or skilled nursing facility (SNF), if billed, must be included in the facility's related consolidated inpatient claim. Charges for transportation of an inpatient will only be considered for reimbursement within the adjudication of the inpatient stay itself. In some situations, Humana determines that, though transportation was medically necessary, the mode of transportation may not have been medically necessary, such as transportation by air. When Humana determines that transportation was medically necessary, but air transportation was not medically necessary, Humana allows ground ambulance rates for the transportation. Generally, reimbursement for ambulance mileage to a facility is limited to the distance from the place from which the patient was transported to the nearest appropriate facility. However, when Humana authorizes admission to a facility in advance, regardless of whether prior authorization is required, Humana reimburses for mileage for the related ambulance transportation to that facility. A provider should bill all of the coverable mileage with HCPCS code A0425, A0435 or A0436. However, if a provider bills such mileage with HCPCS code A0888, Humana will not reimburse that charge but will deny it to provider liability. If the facility did not obtain prior authorization from Humana for the related admission, a provider should bill mileage for transportation beyond the closest facility with HCPCS code A0888. Humana will not reimburse that charge but will deny it to provider liability. Humana adjusts reimbursement of covered transportation and mileage charges when multiple patients are simultaneously transported in the same ambulance to the same destination, indicated by modifier GM. If two patients are transported, Humana allows 75 percent of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for transportation and 50 percent of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for mileage.

rules.Policy_Rule_Text: Providers must bill appropriate modifiers with ambulance charges. Ambulance origin and destination modifiers are billed with both the transportation and mileage charges. When reporting ambulance origin and destination modifiers, the first letter represents the place of origin, and the second letter represents the destination. If a patient is pronounced dead after the ambulance is dispatched but before being loaded on board, providers must report modifier QL with the transportation charge rather than ambulance origin and destination modifiers. In such circumstances, mileage is not covered. However, if providers report the mileage charge, it must be billed with modifier QL, and it is not reimbursed. If multiple patients are simultaneously transported in the same ambulance to the same destination, providers must report modifier GM with the transportation and mileage charges. Providers must bill the ZIP code of the point of pickup (POP). For transportation for less than 100 miles, ambulance mileage may be reported in fractional units to the nearest tenth of a mile. When more than one hospital-to-hospital ambulance service is provided on the same day, the provider must submit a charge for each segment of transportation on a separate claim line with a unit of 1.
